test_title: PYST 48: SSC GD Constable - English (Held On - 21 Feb, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

I feel they are **watching me too closely and making me feel uncomfortable** in the new college.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Breathing down one’s neck.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Breathing down one’s neck"** means watching someone very closely and making them feel uncomfortable. (किसी को बहुत पास से देखना और असहज महसूस कराना)

 
 
• **Example: **My boss has been breathing down my neck to finish the project on time.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Breathing down one’s neck.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Break a leg **(शुभकामनाएं देना): A phrase used to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance.

 
 
• **Example:** Before the play started, we all told the actors to break a leg.
 
 
 
• **In the dark **(अनजान होना): Being unaware or uninformed about something.
 
 
• **Example:** He was kept in the dark about the company's decision to lay off employees.
 
 
 
• **Run out of steam **(उत्साह या ऊर्जा खोना): To lose energy or enthusiasm.
 
 
• **Example:** After working non-stop for eight hours, I finally ran out of steam.
